relations.statement: A lift candidate that is licensed requires replay availability, reduction and closure; a missing new carrier blocks licensing.
relations.hypotheses: L is a PrimitiveLiftCandidate.LiftCandidate; for the blocking part, L.hasNewCarrier = false

relations.statement: A licensed lift candidate requires replay, reduction and closure evidence.
An extension is one-step iff it adds exactly one primitive capability beyond the six-operation spine; extensions adding several (branching, matching, rewriting) are refused as one-step.
relations.hypotheses: A capability count for each extension is declared; the spine arrows mention, supply, designation, admission, retention, internal operation are left as given, with undefined arrows undefined.

lemmas.statement: For each of the four extensions (declarative distinctness, conditional deletion, insertion, substitution), the capability count is greater than 1, so none is one-step.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem four_ext_not_one_step (caps : Fin 4 → Nat) (h : ∀ i, 2 ≤ caps i) : ∀ i, caps i ≠ 1 := by intro i; have := h i; omega

lemmas.statement: A lift candidate without a new carrier is not licensed.

near_misses.claim: Any of the four extensions is a one-step extension because it adds no new glyphs and no counting.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: One-step means exactly one primitive capability; each extension needs several undeclared capabilities (branching, matching, rewriting).

near_misses.claim: A single act (datum, form or instance) separates from the empty state in the two-flag admission model.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Only form then instance separates from the empty state in the declared two-flag model.

open_obligations: No existing declaration was found for the two-flag admission model of Paper000.lean in SRC, so it is not cited.
The capability count per extension is not grounded in a cited declaration.
The undefined spine arrows are deliberately left undefined.
Generators for the six-operation spine are not grounded in SRC and are omitted.
L1 skeleton is a placeholder over hypothetical counts.
